catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class carries a complete sensor_msgs/msg/LaserScan sample. cap.sensing.point_cloud.v1 requires a sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2 artifact, and this node publishes only LaserScan. The extension declares an inline read-only output schema for the complete scan, including the ranges and intensities arrays.

notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware, ROS graph, rosbridge connection, serial port or YDLIDAR node was attached or run, and no hardware run is claimed. RosDriver refuses every hardware backend without a human hardware review at any risk; the card's publish_review is required and the upstream license is NOASSERTION, so this package is not a publication claim.

No preflight section for this exact package and pin was present in the two named ros-wave-b PREFLIGHT.md files. The card's family-config decision and RosDriver helper match the pinned C++ ROS 2 topic interface; entry_symbols is empty and no Python native class is declared, so there was no entry symbol to verify. No native.py or fixtures are used; the only package backend factory is .fake:FakeYdlidarRos2. A hardware deployment would use the RosDriver helper's lazy rosbridge WebSocket and requires an operator-run rosbridge, a supplied ws/wss endpoint with the resolved /scan topic, and a human-signed driver.lock.json reviewed_by entry; this package supplies no default destination. The clone was left unmodified (G1 passed); no network, pip install, upstream execution or hardware backend was used.

Interface: the pinned node is a plain rclcpp::Node named ydlidar_node (src/ydlidar_node.cpp:60) that creates a sensor_msgs::msg::LaserScan publisher on the relative topic name scan with SensorDataQoS (src/ydlidar_node.cpp:179; type include at :25). The launch file gives the node the root namespace / (launch/ydlidar_launch.py:44), and README shows /scan (README.md:36), so this package configures the resolved endpoint /scan and keeps source_name "scan". A deployment that starts the node under another namespace or remaps the topic must expose the corresponding resolved endpoint. The launch file uses the old LifecycleNode action, but the pinned source is a plain node; this package binds no lifecycle transition and does not claim managed lifecycle behavior. QoS selection is not modeled by the rosbridge helper; the subscription uses the broker default and no QoS match is claimed.

Capability: x-cap.adlink-ros.laserscan.v1 (verb read, operation subscribe) subscribes to one fresh LaserScan and maps the complete message: header.frame_id, header.stamp.sec/nanosec, angle_min, angle_max, angle_increment, scan_time, time_increment, range_min, range_max, ranges and intensities. The full ranges and intensities arrays are carried; this is not metadata-only coverage. No catalogue class fits: cap.sensing.point_cloud.v1 requires a sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2 artifact and this node publishes LaserScan, not PointCloud2. The capability is recorded in catalogue_requests. The generated REFERENCE.md summarizes the read-verb extension under Measures using its first unit-bearing required output field (stamp_sec); the served output schema in the manifest and MCP projection carries all twelve fields, including both arrays.

Fake: ROS-free F0 contract fake (the SDK's RecordingRosTransport base class with a canned handler; it does not replay captured traffic). It answers /scan with a placeholder LaserScan and models a silent topic, an unrelated subscription id, a failed subscription and malformed/missing fields. The ranges and intensities arrays are five placeholder elements, not a device size: the upstream computes the real length at run time as (max_angle - min_angle)/angle_increment + 1 (src/ydlidar_node.cpp:205-207) from the configured angle span and the device's angular increment; no fixed array size is stated in the clone. The default max_message_bytes is 1 MiB (a client execution bound, not a device limit); a scan larger than that would be refused by the transport, and live message sizes require deployment validation. The fake's values are test data and are never Facts, Limits or refs.

Safety: observational sensor at R0 (the card floor). The node exposes no application service, action, stop or reset path; this package exposes no actuation, write or safe-state action and declares no Limit or site-limits overlay. The stock e-stop is software-only: the SDK latches and records safe_state_achieved true because there is no actuating capability; that is not a native or physical stop, and no estop_physical_ref is claimed. The clone does not state an optical hazard class, so this package makes no laser-class claim; its scope is data observation. Extension read-verb capabilities are not a latch exemption: after the software latch the x-cap read is refused with MHS.SAFETY.ESTOP_ENGAGED, which the tests exercise.

Tests and warnings: test_driver.py keeps check_driver and adds ten repository cases covering the complete output, endpoint/type/queue, a fresh subscription per read, no publish/advertise, silent/wrong-id/failed/malformed replies, the software-only e-stop and the post-latch refusal. The final gate run's only warning is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE: the driver declares no actuating limit, so SAFE-014 has nothing to probe while every other CL3 test passed. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. The upstream node's actual port, baud, device model, laser class, scan length and QoS are operator/deployment facts outside this package.

NOT COVERED: the hardware backend and live ROS behavior; the upstream node's serial-port/baud/model parameters and any parameter write (the node reads them at startup and this package exposes no write path); the raw header stamp is returned as sec/nanosec, not converted to RFC 3339; the built-in ROS parameter services; QoS; and any claimed physical laser hazard class.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the /scan binding (relative 'scan' LaserScan publisher of the plain node ydlidar_node in the launch file's root namespace: src/ydlidar_node.cpp:60, 179, launch/ydlidar_launch.py:44), the ROS 2 stamp fields and complete output mapping, the software-only e-stop of this passive R0 sensor, the fake, the tests, the provenance and all ten facts. Four facts said more than their lines: the main-loop fact stated the initialisation condition from a range starting after it, the stamp fact named the frame_id parameter where the lines show a local variable, the array fact called the std::ceil index 'rounded', and the frame_id fact claimed an ordering outside its range. The reviewer corrected them (the loop fact now cites 174-216) and added six facts (shutdown after the loop, the SDK's 0.0 for ignored and invalid ranges, and the licence statements: Apache 2.0 in package.xml and the launch header, a BSD text for the vendored SDK) in driver.py, updated facts.md (a 0.0 range is not a distance; a failed initialisation leaves /scan silent) and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged (sha256:00f2c24de6fcf6009297a63d4b8525d42ab4932537c719f33c9a76fa401746e0). The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Passive serial 2-D lidar publisher at R0; the clone states no laser class, so confirm the unit's Class 1 label. The node publishes with rclcpp::SensorDataQoS() (best effort); the rosbridge subscription must match it. A 0.0 range marks an empty array slot, an ignored angle or an invalid range, not an obstacle at 0 m. If initialize() or turnOn() fails, the node exits without publishing and every read times out. The README documents range_min/range_max parameters while the node declares min_range/max_range (src/ydlidar_node.cpp:114-118), so the README names have no effect. Licence: no top-level licence file; package.xml and the launch header say Apache 2.0 and the vendored SDK carries a BSD text; the card's NOASSERTION and publish_review required stand.
